questions.question:

questions.referenceSection: Related supplied handout: L-1-Anatomical Directions & Movement.pdf; pages 2, 3. Read the page-map clarification where supplied wording is simplified.
questions.explanation:
A standard reference posture: upright, facing forward, upper limbs at the sides with palms forward.
Example: A teacher describes the thumb as lateral even when a model turns its hand.
Key distinction: Reference terminology remains tied to anatomical position rather than the observer's changing viewpoint.

sources.title: OpenStax — Anatomy and Physiology 2e: Types of Body Movements
sources.use: Open textbook reference for standard movement terminology and joint examples.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf — Anatomy, Head and Neck, Nose Paranasal Sinuses
sources.use: Further reading for nasal and sinus anatomy. Some direct NCBI pages were access-limited; available records and excerpts were checked rather than claiming complete chapter access.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf — Anatomy, Head and Neck, Temporomandibular Joint
sources.use: Regional reference for TMJ anatomy. Accessible records/excerpts complement the supplied slides; full-page access was restricted during checking.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf — Anatomy, Head and Neck, Tongue
sources.use: Regional reference for tongue anatomy and innervation; accessible excerpts checked.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf — Palatoglossus Muscle
sources.use: Supports the standard vagal motor exception for palatoglossus.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf — Anatomy, Head and Neck, Pharynx
sources.use: Regional reference for further study, with available indexing/excerpts used within access limits.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf — Anatomy, Thorax, Esophagus
sources.use: Regional reference and accessible excerpts for course, relations and functional anatomy; level/distance estimates are treated as approximate.

sources.title: Elsevier Complete Anatomy — Esophagus
sources.use: Publisher anatomy resource for the mediastinal course and a three-constriction convention; complements four-site teaching schemes.

sources.title: AAO-HNSF — Clinical Practice Guideline: Nosebleed (Epistaxis)
sources.use: Professional guideline route for interpreting the management slides. Procedures and medications are not presented as universal self-treatment instructions.

sources.title: NHS — Nosebleed
sources.use: Public first-aid and escalation guidance. Anatomy examples do not replace local clinical assessment.

sources.title: Woodruff's plexus—arterial or venous?
sources.use: Review documenting inconsistent literature about this historical label; the course distinguishes it from a universal posterior arterial source.

sources.title: ASHA — Adult Dysphagia
sources.use: Professional reference supporting distinctions between functional stages, airway entry and evidence needed for swallowing assessment.

sources.title: NIDCD — What Is Hoarseness?
sources.use: Official educational reference for voice symptoms and the need to distinguish causes from a symptom alone.
